content: The work on Arabic offensive language detection is relatively nascent BIBREF16, BIBREF17, BIBREF18, BIBREF19, BIBREF5. Mubarak et al. mubarak2017abusive suggested that certain users are more likely to use offensive languages than others, and they used this insight to build a list of offensive Arabic words and they constructed a labeled set of 1,100 tweets. Abozinadah et al. abozinadah2017detecting used supervised classification based on a variety of features including user profile features, textual features, and network features. They reported an accuracy of nearly 90%. Alakrot et al. alakrot2018towards used supervised classification based on word unigrams and n-grams to detect offensive language in YouTube comments. They improved classification with stemming and achieved a precision of 88%. Albadi et al. albadi2018they focused on detecting religious hate speech using a recurrent neural network. Further; Schmidt and Wiegand schmidt-wiegand-2017-survey surveyed major works on hate speech detection; Fortuna and Nunes Fortuna2018Survey provided a comprehensive survey for techniques and works done in the area between 2004 and 2017.
